chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Musawir, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “Beware of publicizing it. By Allah, your Imam will surely go into ghaybah for years of your time, and you will surely be tested and purified until it is said: He died, he was killed, he perished, in which valley did he travel? And the eyes of the believers will surely shed tears over him, and you will surely be overturned as ships are overturned in the waves of the sea.”

Then none will be saved except one whose covenant Allah has taken, and in whose heart He has written faith, and whom He has supported with a spirit from Him. And twelve confusing banners will surely be raised, such that it will not be known which is which.

He said: So I wept, then I said: So what should we do? He said: Then he looked at sunlight entering the veranda and said: O Abu Abdillah, do you see this sun? I said: Yes. He said: By Allah, our matter is clearer than this sun.

key_terms.إِمَامُكُمْ: your Imam, the divinely appointed leader of the community
key_terms.التَّنْوِيهَ: publicizing or drawing attention to the matter
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: faith firmly established in the heart
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers who remain faithful through the trial
key_terms.رَايَةً مُشْتَبِهَةً: a confusing banner or claim that resembles truth and causes uncertainty
key_terms.رُوحٍ: a spirit from Allah by which the believer is strengthened
key_terms.لَتُمَحَّصُنَّ: you will surely be tested and sifted thoroughly
key_terms.مِيثَاقَهُ: His covenant, denoting divine binding commitment and selection

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) say about the trials and confusion during the ghaybah of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the severe trial of the Imam’s ghaybah, during which believers will face confusion, grief, and competing claims. It teaches that salvation in that period belongs to those firmly established in iman by Allah, while affirming that the truth of the Ahl al-Bayt’s matter remains utterly clear despite the confusion of people.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muhammad Bin Al Musawir, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Beware of the allusions! But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Your Imam<sup>asws</sup> would be absent (in Occultation) for years from your time. You will be Sifted until it would be said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> died, killed, perished, (Don’t know) by which valley he<sup>asws</sup> travelled’, and the eyes of the Momineen would shed tears upon him<sup>asws</sup>, and you would be tossed around like the tossing of the ships in the waves of the sea.

Thus, he would not attain salvation except the one whose Covenant Allahazwj has Taken, and Written the Eman in his heart, and Aided him by a Spirit from Himazwj. And you would be separating into twelve resembling banners, not known which one is from which’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I wept, then I said, ‘So how should we deal with it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the sunshine entering the pavilion and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Abdullah! Do you see this sunshine?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Our<sup>asws</sup> matter would be clearer that this sunshine’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran from Muhammad ibn al-Musawir from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following.

“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say as herein below. “Beware of publicity. By Allah, your Imam will disappear from the public sight for years of your time and you will be sifted until the only thing that could be said about his would be, “He is dead, killed, destroyed and no one would know in which of the valleys he may have travelled. The eyes of the faithful ones will weep for him and you will be turned upside down just the ships face the rough seas and choppy waters.

No one will survive this except those from whom Allah has taken a covenant, written faith in his hear and has supported him with an spirit from His self. You will come to know of twelve similar flags and one would not be able find which is whiCh”

The narrator has said, “I then wept and then said, “Whatshall we do?” The Imam (a.s.) then looked to the sun (light) on the deck and said, ‘O abu ‘Abdallah, our case, (Leadership with Divine Authority) is more clear than the sun (light) on the deck.”
